title: Learning banjo from Nathaniel Morris and finding his own style
summary: Studied banjo with Nathaniel Morris and David Jones, practised on his own, and says he plays his own ideas, not Charlie Parker's.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: That's right. I could walk back. I lived more and after we moved off to Constantinople, I lived more and general Taylor's. Right where that was right around the corner. I wasn't too far away. And what about the banjo? How did you learn the banjo? Well, I have a few ideas. I had a friend of mine, Nathaniel Morris. He was a great banjoist. Who? Nathaniel Morris. He has a son that's great, two sons, at least great drummers. One of them they call, what that boy, I can't call his name. He's up in St. Louisville. He's up in St. Louis now. Well, he was a good musician. And I used to go to him and take lessons from him. Well, I have a few ideas about it because I used to play ukulele. I had good ideas about it. So I took lessons from him for a while. Then Kimmel used to come out and back from my house and sit out there and give me ideas and all that too. Well, what sort of ideas would they give you? Well, just showing your dick and finger in the higher bill cards and all that too. You know? Huh? You studied comedy then, some? Yeah. On your own? On my own, yeah. On my own. Yeah, I studied on my own. Well, I knew music already. But all I had to learn was the fingers. And David Jones would tell me all the time, you go home, you practice your music. But forget about it. Put it aside. Knowing out of your head. Knowing how you call it, just out of your head. And that's what I do. But I was going to take lessons during the same time. Manuel Sells was playing with the band with David Jones, but he was taking lessons too. Sam there as I was there, he would be there. But he was already playing with that orchestra. That was a rest of the band. He was working with the band. I was playing with the band. I was playing with the band. I was playing with the band. I was playing with the band.
How did you really get into playing? Was it mainly through the lessons? Did you work out some of your own ideas? How do you do that?

Well, I have a lot of ideas. I don't try, if I can't help it, from trying to follow behind some other guys. I try to work my own way, but everybody say now, it seems like I'm copying behind Charlie Parker, which I think. But I don't play style on Charlie Parker, but I try to play. I like to play music, but I like to play in a certain swing, a certain way. You see? I got ideas. I use my own ideas at times.
